territorial_scope.description: Amends the federal criminal code of the United States, so it applies nationally to conduct prosecuted under title 18.

evidence.quote: Section 2252A(c) of title 18, United States Code, is amended—

summary.short: Amends federal criminal law (18 U.S.C. 2252A, 2256) to remove the affirmative defense for AI-produced child pornography and add simulated obscene exhibition of genitals, pubic area, buttocks or female nipple to sexually explicit conduct. Includes a severability clause. No effective date is stated.
summary.long: The bill amends title 18 of the United States Code, the federal criminal code, in two places. Section 2(a) strikes paragraph (2) of section 2252A(c) and the sentence that barred the affirmative defense for child pornography described in section 2256(8)(C). Section 2(b) amends the definition of sexually explicit conduct in section 2256(2)(B) to add a clause (iv) covering actual or simulated obscene exhibition of the clothed or unclothed genitals, pubic area, buttocks, or female nipple. The text does not itself set penalties and states no effective date or compliance period. Section 2(c) is a severability clause preserving the remaining provisions if any part is held unconstitutional. The short title is the Protecting Our Children in an AI World Act of 2025. In this text the bill is at the introduced stage.
